<reason>B narrowly wins on the comparative motion. A expressly accepts fund-style oversight for reserve-investing issuers, encompassing the principal operating examples debated. Its cash-only alternative and compliance-cost argument support tailored requirements or exceptions, but do not establish that issuers generally belong closer to ordinary software projects. A nevertheless handled pressure better and exposed significant weaknesses: B’s nonexistent Tether collapse, unsupported counterfactual, and exaggerated claims that only prudential supervision could prevent failures. Those errors substantially narrow B’s victory.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s closing applies A’s investment-activity trigger to the major issuers, turning an apparent disagreement into substantial agreement with the proposition. A’s response about encouraging safer cash-only architectures preserves a meaningful exception, but does not overturn that central concession.</best_rebuttal>
